In ancient medieval times Pradvivaka was the advisor to the king in this department?
x:
The Pradvivaka (Pradvivaka or Pradvivakudu) was the chief judicial adviser to the king in ancient and medieval Indian administration. He assisted the ruler in legal matters, interpreted Dharmashastra, advised on judicial decisions and supervised the administration of justice. His position was equivalent to that of a chief judge or legal expert in the royal court. Several ancient legal texts refer to the office of the Pradvivaka as an important component of judicial administration.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
